thread.title: Chip Maker TSMC Breaks Sales Record on Bitcoin Mining Boost

title: Chip Maker TSMC Breaks Sales Record on Bitcoin Mining Boost
text:
Main » Chip Maker TSMC Breaks Sales Record on Bitcoin Mining Boost Chip Maker TSMC Breaks Sales Record on Bitcoin Mining Boost 20 April 2018 
Along with weak results from Philip Morris and Procter & Gamble Co (PG.N), defensive sectors such as consumer staples.SPLRCS were also hurt by a rise in US 10-year Treasury yields, which helped bank stocks. 
Chip and chip-equipment stocks beyond Asia had fallen on the news. 
A warning from Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) (2330.TW), the world's largest contract chipmaker and an Apple Inc (AAPL.O) supplier, on soft demand for smartphones and on the industry's growth this year sparked a tumble in chip stocks and made Apple the S&P's second biggest weight. Shares of Japanese semiconductor equipment and silicon wafer makers, including Tokyo Electron Ltd and Alps Electric Co, also fell. Apple was the biggest drag on the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nasdaq. European chip stocks also weakened, with Dialog Semiconductor PLC declining 4% and STMicroelectronics NV dropping 3.3%. 
The S&P consumer staples sector.SPLRCS declined 3.2 percent as Philip Morris plunged 17.4 percent after the tobacco company's weak results and forecast. Altria, the parent of Philip Morris USA, fell 6 percent. 
TSMC shares in NY fell 6 percent on the news. 
QUALCOMM, Inc . (NASDAQ: QCOM) down 2.4 percent. 
Still, not everything was gloomy. 
Micron Technology, Inc . (NASDAQ: MU) down 1.8 percent. American Express (AXP.N) was up 3.6 percent after the credit card issuer easily topped Wall Street profit estimates. 
"What's happening in this season is even if you meet, that's not good enough, you've got to beat convincingly", said JJ Kinahan, chief market strategist at TD Ameritrade in Chicago. TSMC provides mining hardware manufacturer Bitmain its ASIC chips, and it appears the success of the Antminer E3 may have something to do with the continued growth, as 41 percent of the Q1 earnings occurred in March. Among them AMD ( AMD.O ) and Nvidia ( NVDA.O ) fell about 1.6 percent, while Intel (INTC.O) was off 0.4 percent. 
Data provider TrendForce had earlier estimated 2018 global smartphone production at around 1.5 billion units, 2.8 percent up on 2017 but down from a previously expected 5 percent. 
The S&P 500 posted 22 new 52-week highs and 16 new lows; the Nasdaq Composite recorded 87 new highs and 52 new lows. Related articles
